subtopics.title: Why City Air Differs from Farm Air

questions.question: Urban surfaces like tar and concrete have low albedo, which means they:
options: Reflect most radiation and stay cool
Reflect little radiation and absorb most of it as heat

questions.question: The city's air is drier than the countryside's mainly because:
options: Cities receive less rainfall than farms
City air is too warm to hold moisture
Rain is drained away off sealed surfaces, leaving little water to evaporate, and vegetation is scarce

questions.question: Wind in a city is best described as:
options: Slower on average than open country, but funnelled into gusty canyons between tall buildings
Always faster than in open country

questions.question: Cities are slightly cloudier and rainier than surrounding farmland partly because they:
options: Release convection from the heat island and exhale condensation nuclei around which droplets form

subtopics.title: The Urban Heat Island — Definition and Causes

questions.question: An urban heat island is:
options: An island city surrounded by warm ocean
A park inside a hot city
A heat wave that strikes cities only
The dome of warmer air over a city, with temperatures noticeably higher than surrounding rural areas

questions.question: The heat island effect peaks:
options: At night and in winter, over the dense city centre
At midday in summer, over the suburbs

questions.question: The dips over parks in the urban temperature profile prove that:
options: Vegetation cools its surroundings through shading and transpiration

questions.question: Urban canyons intensify the heat island because vertical walls:
options: Trap radiation by reflecting it wall to wall into the street, and narrow the sky window through which streets cool at night

subtopics.title: Heat Island Effects and How Cities Cool Themselves

questions.question: Hot city nights during heat waves are dangerous because they:
options: Deny the body its overnight recovery period, raising heat-stress illness among the vulnerable

questions.question: In South African cities, the residents worst exposed to heat island effects are:
options: People under zinc roofs in informal housing, where a shack becomes an oven

questions.question: Painting roofs white or light colours reduces the heat island by:
options: Raising albedo so more radiation is reflected instead of absorbed

questions.question: Street trees are the premier cooling strategy because each tree:
options: Cools twice — shading the surface below and transpiring, so energy is spent on evaporation instead of heating

subtopics.title: The Pollution Dome and the Pollution Plume

questions.question: The difference between a pollution dome and a pollution plume is:
options: The dome is industrial and the plume is domestic
A dome forms over the city in calm conditions; wind stretches the same pollution downwind into a plume
The plume forms first and becomes a dome

questions.question: A winter temperature inversion seals the dome over the city because rising smoke:
options: Is blown back down by wind
Reaches the warm layer aloft, loses its buoyancy and spreads sideways as under a ceiling

questions.question: The Highveld's brown winter haze is deepened by the Kalahari High because its subsiding air:
options: Lays a persistent upper inversion lid over the plateau
Adds dust from the Kalahari desert

questions.question: Which strategy pair correctly matches source-cutting with weather-wise management?
options: More coal stoves; burning on calm days
Electrification of homes and stack scrubbers; no open burning on stable winter days
Painting roofs white; building in valleys

subtopics.title: The City Is a Storage Heater

questions.question: The storage heater picture says a city:
options: Soaks up sunshine in its dark materials all day and breathes the heat back out at night
Heats up only when electricity is used
Cools faster than farmland at night

questions.question: The maize field stays cooler than the city because the field:
options: Sweats — its soil and plants spend solar energy on evaporation instead of heating the air

questions.question: The city cannot sweat because:
options: Its air is too dry to hold vapour
Rain is hustled off sealed roofs and roads into drains, leaving nothing to evaporate

subtopics.title: Cooling the Island — Undo Each Cause

questions.question: The sins-reversed method for the strategies question means:
options: Taking each cause of the heat island and proposing the action that directly undoes it

questions.question: The black T-shirt comparison explains why:
options: Dark city surfaces should be replaced or painted with light, reflective colours

questions.question: Permeable paving and urban wetlands cool the city by:
options: Keeping water in the city so evaporation — and its cooling — can resume

questions.question: Cooling the city is called a justice project because:
options: Heat kills selectively — the elderly, infants and residents of zinc-roofed informal housing suffer first

questions.question: In the pot-lid picture, the lid over the winter city is:
options: The temperature inversion — warm air resting on cold, stopping rising smoke
A layer of dust from mines

questions.question: The one-line dome-versus-plume rule is:
options: Calm makes a dome; wind makes a plume
Wind makes a dome; calm makes a plume
Domes form in summer; plumes in winter
Domes are clean; plumes are dirty

questions.question: The pollution dome is thickest over the poorest communities because:
options: Homes there must burn coal and wood for warmth, feeding smoke directly into the sealed winter air

questions.question: Since the winter inversion cannot be removed, all dome-reduction strategies aim to:
options: Break up the inversion with aircraft
Make less smoke and time emissions wisely — cleaner home energy, stack filters, no open burning on still days, industry sited downwind
